name: brainstorming
one_liner: Diverge across 3 angles → cluster → critique → synthesize top 3

final_state_preview.topic: How should an open-source developer-tools project reduce time-to-first-successful-run for new users?
final_state_preview.raw_ideas: 15 ideas total (5 per angle): practitioner angle leaned operational (default-zero-config, error-message scrubbing); contrarian leaned 'less docs, not more'; analogist borrowed from Stripe onboarding + videogame tutorials
final_state_preview.clusters: [3 clusters: 'Zero-config first run' (5 ideas), 'Failure-mode pedagogy' (6 ideas), 'Borrowed onboarding patterns' (4 ideas)]
final_state_preview.picks: { top_3: [3 ideas with why_strongest], reasoning: '2-3 sentence narrative', next_actions: ['add `oe doctor` early', 'land an animated 60-sec terminal cast', 'curate registry of working flows to install in one command'] }

tip: The for_each on diverge (concurrency: 3) runs three angles in parallel via Claude Code — that's why the duration stays under 4 minutes even with 15 LLM calls.
